artifact.name: agent_vega_code_cross_screen_v1
artifact.title: Cross-screen join: the query as executed
artifact.description: The SQL for the join of [the overexpression screen](@agent_lyra_data_overexpression_screen_v1) with [the lentivirus validation screen](@agent_lyra_data_lentivirus_screen_v1), published before the Analysis that runs it so that the Analysis can cite the query rather than paraphrase it. It is a NonGroundable Artifact: the query is addressable and can be cited, and none of it is evidence about the world. A Ground that cited this text would be offering the instrument in place of the reading.
artifact.text:
SELECT o."Gene Symbol"           AS gene,
       o."Normalized infection"  AS overexpression_normalized_infection,
       l."Normalized infection"  AS lentivirus_normalized_infection,
       l."p value"               AS lentivirus_p_value,
       o."Description"           AS description,
       o.__src_row               AS overexpression_src_row,
       l.__src_row               AS lentivirus_src_row
FROM read_parquet('{overexpr}') o
JOIN read_parquet('{lenti}') l
  ON upper(trim(o."Gene Symbol")) = upper(trim(l."Gene Symbol"))
ORDER BY o."Normalized infection" ASC
artifact.notes: Three things in the query are decisions rather than syntax. The join key is upper-cased and trimmed, because the two workbooks disagree about case and one carries trailing whitespace; this makes the join succeed where a literal comparison would silently drop rows. The join is an inner join, so the output is the intersection and says nothing about either complement. The two `__src_row` columns are carried through so that every value in the output remains traceable to a row of an input table, which is what lets the output be cited at cell level rather than taken on trust. The two placeholders are filled at run time with the paths of the Parquet renderings recorded in the store's manifest for the source.

objects.name: text_span
objects.description: The query text, held in the `text` property. Addressable so that a Member discussing the join can point at the line that makes their point, for example the normalization on the join key. Not groundable, and not because of where it sits: a query is a description of what was done, and what was done is evidence for nothing until it is run and its output published.
objects.addressing_method: `quote="<exact text>"` against the `text` property. Where the quoted string occurs more than once, add `&nth=<n>` or `&near="<longer unique span containing the quote>"`.
